open_obligations: Check that the 2^(3q) factor keeps estimators efficient only for constant width q.
Check whether the soundness theorem rules out obfuscation as Buhl et al. define it.
Note the guarantee is average-case, which Brown-Cohen et al. list as a limitation.
out.other_title: Open: does prover-estimator debate avoid obfuscation, and are its debaters poly-time?
out.rationale: Buhl et al. list as open whether prover-estimator debate avoids obfuscation and whether its debaters can be built in polynomial time. Theorem 6.1 (soundness) gives, for every prover, an estimator among circuits of size O(q 2^(3q) n d^2 / eta^2) with oracle access to the prover that caps a dishonest prover's payoff, and stresses that stability is needed only for completeness; the size bound is exponential in width q, so polynomial size needs q constant.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether prover-estimator debate avoids obfuscated arguments and how large the honest estimator must be

text: Theorem 6.1 (soundness) states that, with B the set of circuits of size O(q 2^(3q) n d^2 / eta^2) that may query the prover's strategy at each gate, for every prover strategy A there is an estimator B in that set whose expected payoff to A over inputs is at most P[A(x) = L(x)]/rho^(d+1) + eta. The authors stress that A-provability and stability are needed only for completeness, so a dishonest prover offering an unstable decomposition into hard queries must still lose to B.
title: Theorem 6.1 soundness: efficient estimator caps a dishonest prover's payoff
